w: During the evening assembly Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was carried in a palanquin by children. Dancing boys welcomed the Lord and Swamishri into the special Children's Day program. A drama presentation depicted a Bal parayan, dances and Children's forum activities. Finally Swamishri blessed the Satsang assembly.

While Swamishri was performing his morning puja, Balmukund Swami performed the mahapuja. In conclusion Swamishri performed the arti of Harikrishna Maharaj and blessed the devotees. Swamishri then visited the kitchen and areas where the food items for Annakut festival were being prepared and arranged. Swamishri blessed the festival assembly and at 11.30 am sang thal before Thakorji. The Annakut was profusely arranged before Thakorji. Finally, Swamishri performed arti of Thakorji. More than 25,000 devotees came for Annakut darshan. ( Detailed news report )

This day, Kartik sud 11, was special because was on this day Nilkanth Varni had received initiation into the sadhu-fold from Ramanand Swami. Also, on this day, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was given initiation by his guru Shastriji Maharaj.

Today 10 youths received bhagvati diksha and 7 youths received parshad diksha from Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In his blessings Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Some people ask, 'How will sadhus serve society?' They feel sadhus are a burden. But they are not a burden. They travel from village-to-village and serve people. They redeem people from addictions and lead them onto the path of devotion to God. When people are elevated personally, the country as a whole progresses. Society is made up of virtuous individuals. And a virtuous society leads to an affluent country. Sadhus will help to create such virtuous individuals."

At 10.00 a.m. Swamishri departed from Pindvada and arrived at another work site in Sivera village, 12 km away. Swamishri observed the stone carvings and sculptings. As he walked through the workshop, Swamishri showered flower petals and blessed the artisans. Thereafter he addressed the assembly of craftsmen in Hindi.
Swamishri stopped over at Jadoli village where the mandir stone sculpting projects for BAPS mandirs are in progress. On returning to Pindvada, Swamishri visited the Sanstha's workshops.
At 7.00 p.m. Swamishri presided over a public satsang assembly in the town center and blessed the assembly in Hindi.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - Sivera, 15 November 2003
w: Swamishri visits the BAPS workshops where stones are cut and carved for the Akshardham project in New Delhi and for mandir projects in Houston and Chicago. In the workshops Swamishri blessed the craftsmen and workers.

The evening assembly to celebrate the BAPS Centenary Year was held at the Racecourse Ground. The assembly was based on the theme “In the joy of others lies our own”. The stage backdrop comprised a giant replica of Akshar Deri enshrining the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj along with huge photographic scenes of both Swaminarayan Akshardhams, in Delhi and Gandhinagar. Viveksagar Swami first addressed the assembly. Then Dr Swami spoke on BAPS’ spiritual and secular activities. Two videos on Akshardham and Pramukh Swami Maharaj were shown. Then the senior sadhus, devotees and guests honoured Swamishri with flower garlands. Children performed a cultural dance. To crown the assembly Swamishri blessed the huge gathering of 20,000 devotees and well-wishers, “Because of I-ness and Mine-ness one experiences pain and unhappiness in life. If they are dissolved then one experiences the divine joy of God. One must first understand that one’s true form is atma, and within it resides Paramatma. When God leaves from within then nothing will work. No matter how intelligent one may be nothing will be possible through one’s own effort.” In conclusion more than 20,000 devotees and guests performed arti. The celebration ended with a spectacular fireworks display.
17 devotees pilgrimaged by foot from Bhadra; 17 male and 27 female devotees pilgrimaged by foot.

At 4.45 p.m. Swamishri departed from Bochasan and travelled 235 km to Sankari. En route, devotees of Vasad, Dabhoi, Rajpipla, Netrang, Mandvi and Kadol had assembled by the roadside for darshan. Swamishri arrived at the BAPS mandir in Sankari at 8.35 p.m., after travelling for 3 hours and 50 minutes. Swamishri was briefly welcomed with garlands.

This morning after breakfast, the sadhus came to Mahant Swami Maharaj's room to show him the outline of the evening programme of the children's shibir. They told Swamishri, "In today's assembly, the 13 main festivals that come during the whole year are to be celebrated in your presence. One of them is a symbolic festival of murti installation."

Hearing this, Swamishri then and there took the anjan shalaka in his hand and began to touch it to the chests of all the sadhus and devotees present in the room, as if installing a murti in the mandir of their hearts!
Seeing this, the sadhus asked, "While touching the anjan shalaka to the chests of the sadhus and devotees, what were you thinking?"
"Yogibapa," Swamishri said.
"Meaning?"
"I was placing in you the Yogibapa who is within me," Swamishri said.
All who heard this were overwhelmed by his power and grace.

This morning Mahant Swami Maharaj woke at 2:30. By 5:05 he had come out of his room. "Oh..." escaped from everyone's lips, but it came to be known that Swamishri had been ready since 4:00. But so early would not suit anyone, so from 4:00 to 5:00, for an hour, he read the book "Purushottam Bolya Prite".
Truly, every incident of Swamishri bears witness that he is different from us.
After the puja was completed, elders came on stage and asked questions, and Mahant Swami Maharaj gave wonderful answers.
Question: "Now we have grown old, so what should we do?"

Swamishri: "Since you have grown old, you should understand, as it says in Swamini Vato: 'Just as the farmer does not feed the old bullock, says Mukta, so everyone insults the old.' (Swamini Vato 6.48) So now that you have aged, however you may be, even if there was respect, it will not remain the same now. You should adjust to them (your sons and daughters). They will not adjust to you. If you live like this, you will worship God in happiness and joy."
Question: "We see strange natures in the family, so what should we do?"

Swamishri: "In the rising generation, natures are rising too. They are of all kinds. Since we have become elders, we should be merciful, be compassionate, and understand that it is bound to be like this. All our lives we have done just the same. Tit for tat... No one will listen to you. Experience is a comb given to a bald man. So do not impose your experience on others, keep it with yourself. When you were young you did not listen to anyone, so these people will not listen either. So do not attempt that."

Question: "For the last 12 years I have been doing seva. Ishwarcharan Swami says that if you do seva you become ekantik. So how should I do seva so that I become ekantik and do not fall away from seva?"

Swamishri: "Do seva with a pure feeling. Let us not expect any honour or anything else. The same action, but with God's name chanted along with it. It is the feeling that has to change. Only for God. Do seva with the pure feeling that 'my dealings are only with God.' Do seva in that way."
Question: "I don't feel like going to the Sunday assembly. What should I do?"

Swamishri: "Keep faith in Yogibapa. He has commanded, 'Whatever happens, attend the Sunday assembly.' If we obey that command even by some device, the work is done. Yogibapa's command means billions of rupees. And household work means five rupees."

Question: "You say that humility is the number one. Without it, all virtues are a stain. But outside, if we do not keep our standing and behave humbly, no one takes any notice and worldly dealings do not get done. So what should we do?"
Swamishri: "This (living humbly) concerns satsang, not elsewhere. In the world, do as is appropriate."
In this way there was a very beautiful question and answer session with Swamishri.
Mahant Swami Maharaj came from the assembly to his residence. Here Harinayandas Swami was standing with Shri Hardikbhai Gajjar. Pointing to Hardikbhai, he said:

"Swami! He has a very big name in virtual effects in the whole of Mumbai. Work for Star TV and others comes to him. He is very close to Arvindbhai Babbal. He came to know that Arvindbhai Babbal had given up cigarettes. In his mind he was absolutely sure that 'Arvind will never give up cigarettes', but he saw it with his own eyes. He also saw the de-addiction film 'Muktanand' made by Arvindbhai. And he himself felt from within, 'I too want to give up cigarettes. And I want to give them up right in front of Swamishri, receiving his blessings.' That is why he has come here."

Showing great pleasure, Swamishri blessed him and made the very same gesture of rubbing both hands together that he had made before Arvindbhai Babbal. "Wah!" escaped from the sadhus' lips: "Now Hardikbhai's addiction is gone!"
Today, seeing Anandviharidas Swami, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "Divyaratna Swami was with you."
Anandviharidas Swami said in surprise, "This goes back to when we were teenagers! He and I were travelling with Swamishri in the vacation after Class 10. Even I had forgotten this!"
The treasury of Swamishri's memory always seems inexhaustible.

Today Manan Kotak, son of Shri Maulikbhai Kotak, owner of Chitralekha, came to meet Mahant Swami Maharaj. He asked Swamishri a question: "What is the reason that you are able to do so much work at the age of 84?"
Gesturing upwards with both hands, Swamishri said, "God!"

After the cheshta singing, seeing Pritamprasaddas Swami, Mahant Swami Maharaj recalled an old memory and said, "In 1971 we went to Ukai to fetch Pritam Swami. Assemblies were held at Dineshbhai Raval's house."
He said something from 45 years ago as naturally as if it had just happened.

st.t: Canadian Minister Honourable Navdeep Bains Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: Honourable Navdeep Bains, Canandian Minister of Innovation, Science & Economic Development, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s ageless beauty, borderless culture and timeless values. Accompanying the ministers was a 10-member delegation.

On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj – Spiritual Head of Swaminarayan Akshardham and BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha – senior sadhus traditionally welcomed Honourable Navdeep Bains and delegation with a garland of flowers, tilaka (vermillion powder) and the tying of the sacred kalva (sacred thread).

After admiring the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate), Minister Bains visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir where they witnessed the world’s ‘Largest Comprehensive Hindu Temple’. They offered their respects and admired the Mandir’s art and architecture.
Minister Bains visited the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that includes 148 life-sized carved stone elephants depicting message of social harmony, peace and spirituality.

The Canadian delegation offered prayers for world peace and harmony by offering ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India on the sacred image of Sri Neelkanth Varni.

Thereafter, the delegation experienced the educational exhibition Sanskruti Vihar – a cultural voyage that sails through 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage, highlighting India’s contributions to humanity through the ages.

Sharing his sentiments at Akshardham, Canadian Minister of Innovation, Science & Economic Development Honourable Navdeep Bains wrote, “Peace and love is a powerful message. Thank you for an amazing and inspirational visit!”
